name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid)
summary: A water-soluble antioxidant and essential cofactor for prolyl/lysyl hydroxylases in collagen synthesis, carnitine and catecholamine production, and non-haem iron absorption.

conditions.label: Deficiency (scurvy)
conditions.description: Without ascorbate, collagen cross-linking fails, weakening connective tissue, blood-vessel walls and bone matrix.

affects.effect: Perifollicular haemorrhage, corkscrew hairs, poor wound healing
affects.detail: Defective collagen makes capillaries fragile; classic signs are perifollicular bleeding, bruising (ecchymoses) and wounds that reopen or heal slowly.

ageModifiers.infant: Infantile scurvy (Barlow disease): irritability, pseudoparalysis from painful subperiosteal haemorrhage and tenderness of the limbs.

affects.effect: Swollen, bleeding gums and loosening teeth
affects.detail: Gingival collagen breaks down, producing spongy, haemorrhagic gums and eventual tooth loss.
Bleeding plus reduced iron absorption contributes to anaemia and fatigue.

affects.effect: Impaired bone matrix and joint bleeding
affects.detail: Osteoid collagen is defective; children may show growth-plate abnormalities and painful haemarthroses.

ageModifiers.child: Subperiosteal haemorrhage and disturbed endochondral ossification cause bone pain and reluctance to move.
